exercise1.prompt: Filtering with Masks: The names that passed

hiddenCases.name: a score exactly on the mark passes
nobody passing gives an empty list

exercise1.hint: Mask the table, then take the name column of what survives and turn it into a list with .tolist().

exercise2.prompt: Filtering with Masks: Account for every row

hiddenCases.name: with nothing missing the third is zero
the three always total the row count
a score on the mark counts as passed

exercise2.hint: Count the missing ones with .isna().sum() first, then the two comparisons. A comparison is never True for NaN, so those rows fall out of both and have to be counted separately.

choices: The rows where the condition is True
questions.explain: The mask is per row, so the whole row survives or none of it does.

questions.prompt: Which operators combine two conditions on a DataFrame?
questions.explain: Python’s and wants a single truth value; the brackets are needed because & binds tighter than the comparisons.

questions.prompt: A row has NaN in the column you are filtering on. Where does it end up?
choices: In neither the filter nor its opposite
questions.explain: A comparison with NaN is never True, so the two halves do not add up to the whole table.
The readable way to say "everything except", and easier to check than rewriting the condition backwards.
